text: Identity Governance and Administration, or IGA, is the product category built to automate everything this chapter has covered - joiner/mover/leaver lifecycle, access certification campaigns, and separation-of-duties enforcement - across every system in an organization, at a scale no manual process can sustain.

IGA is distinct from plain IAM, which handles authentication - logging someone in - and from PAM, which handles elevated admin credentials specifically. IGA sits on top of both, focused on governance: not can this person log in, but should this person have the access they currently have, and who's accountable for that decision.

The core value comes from connectors - pre-built integrations into HR systems, directory services, and target applications like ERPs and cloud platforms. With that connectivity, the platform builds one continuously updated picture of who has access to what, everywhere - the exact inventory gap that made Maria's untracked SQL Server login invisible, and that made David's leftover AP access hard to spot by eye.

A small organization can run a version of this manually, in spreadsheets, and it works at small scale. It breaks down as systems and users grow: JML automation fires across every connected system at once instead of relying on an admin remembering each one individually; certification campaigns get auto-routed, tracked, and auto-revoked on deadline instead of emailed around and chased down by hand; and SoD enforcement checks a person's entire access footprint continuously instead of someone manually cross-referencing permission lists.

None of this replaces human judgment - a manager still makes the keep or revoke call, a resource owner still decides if a flagged conflict is a real risk. SailPoint and Saviynt are two real, widely deployed vendors in this space, built around exactly that combination: connectors, a live access inventory, scheduled campaigns, and continuous SoD checking. That closes out identity governance - Chapter 7 turns to engineering security controls as code, starting with Lesson 25.
